Credits
Tags: courses
Short Description: The number of credits assigned to a course based on the expected student workload, including instructional time and preparation
Credits
UM 8.31.10 Basis for Credit. The basis of a credit shall normally be three hours work; for example, one credit for each lecture or recitation and two hours of preparation, or one credit for each two-hour laboratory and one hour of preparation, or one credit for each three-hour laboratory with no outside preparation, the student workload for an online class shall be equivalent to the in-class and out-of-class work in its face-to-face equivalent. Individual evaluation of courses offering practice in a professional major shall be made by the respective deans to determine non-lecture hour credits and will include at least an equivalent amount of work as required in the definitions cited above.

Grading Method
Tags: courses
Short Description: The method used to assign grades for a course, such as letter grades or S/U.
Grading Method

A grading method in which student performance is evaluated using letter grades from A (Superior) through F (Failure), with each grade assigned a quality point value used to calculate GPA.
8.53.10 Student grades are defined as follows: A – Superior B – Good C – Fair D – Low grade, passing F – Failure 8.53.11 Grades shall be given quality point values as follows: A = 4.00 points A- = 3.70 points B+ = 3.30 points B = 3.00 points B- = 2.70 points C+ = 2.30 points C = 2.00 points C- = 1.70 points D+ = 1.30 points D = 1.00 points F = 0 points U = 0 points U* = not calculated in GPA

Certain courses do not lend themselves to precise grading. For these courses, only S (satisfactory) or U (unsatisfactory) is given to all students enrolled. S/U courses are labeled as such in the course descriptions in this catalog. S/U courses are not counted as courses taken under the Pass-Fail option.
D1 is the only General Education outcome that can be graded using S/U or Letter Grades. All other outcomes must be graded by Letter Grades.

Curricular Contacts Directory
This directory identifies the individuals and roles involved in the curricular process across the University. Use it to find the appropriate contact for questions, reviews, approvals, or other steps in the curriculum process.
Names are listed alphabetically by first name. You can also filter the directory by role, college, department, college- or department-level approval role, or Faculty Senate role.
All information is manually entered. If you notice any mistakes, or if a role has changed, please email Faculty Senate Specialist Genviéve Spitale (genvieve.spitale@uri.edu).
